executiveSummary: Threat activity against industrial environments remains elevated. Multiple government joint advisories confirm active exploitation of PLCs and industrial access pathways, while edge device zero-days and KEV additions raise near-term risk of IT-to-OT pivot. Supply-chain and webmail abuse further increase identity compromise and operational disruption risk across energy, water, transportation, and manufacturing. Iranian-affiliated actors are actively accessing and tampering with PLCs (Rockwell, Schneider, Siemens), manipulating alarms and programs in US critical infrastructure. Security Advisory China-nexus groups (e.g., Volt Typhoon) are expanding covert SOHO/IoT botnets to pre-position within critical infrastructure, heightening lateral movement risk into OT. Security Advisory Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center has an actively exploited hard‑coded credential backdoor; compromise can erode segmentation protecting OT networks. CISA KEV View Article Fortinet “FortiBleed” credential exposure is enabling domain compromise via FortiGate perimeters; widespread rotation and assessment are required. Security Advisory KEV and weekly bulletins include high-risk OT-adjacent flaws (EVbee DC fast chargers, PcVue HMI/SCADA, DAQFactory HMI project parsing), demanding rapid patching and segmentation. CISA Bulletin CISA Bulletin Pro‑Russia hacktivists are opportunistically compromising internet‑exposed VNC HMIs to alter setpoints and disable alarms; immediate exposure removal is advised. Security Advisory State‑aligned campaigns abusing Zimbra and on‑prem Exchange OWA deliver durable, server‑side persistence and token theft across government and telecom targets. Security Advisory View Article Active exploitation of F5 BIG‑IP APM RCE is impacting remote access gateways frequently used for OT vendor access. Security Advisory

topThreats.title: 1) Active PLC Intrusions (Rockwell/Schneider/Siemens)
topThreats.action: Severity: 5/5 Iranian‑affiliated actors accessed internet‑exposed PLCs and vendor tools to modify logic/AOIs and suppress alarms, causing operational impacts. Energy Water/Wastewater Government Security Advisory

topThreats.title: 2) Cisco Secure FMC Backdoor (KEV)
topThreats.action: Severity: 4/5 Actively exploited hard‑coded credentials in FMC can enable policy tampering that collapses IT/OT isolation; likely chained with auth‑bypass. Perimeter Firewall Mgmt Identity CISA KEV View Article

topThreats.title: 3) FortiBleed: FortiGate Credential Exposure
topThreats.action: Severity: 4/5 Leaked configs and admin hashes enable takeover of FortiGate perimeters and AD abuse; rotate credentials, upgrade hashing, and assess blast radius. VPN Edge Security Advisory

topThreats.title: 4) VNC‑Exposed HMIs Targeted by Hacktivists
topThreats.action: Severity: 4/5 Mass scanning and weak/default creds allow setpoint changes and alarm suppression via VNC; remove exposure and enforce MFA immediately. Water Energy Food/Ag Security Advisory

topThreats.title: 5) EVbee DC‑80 and OT‑Adjacent Critical CVEs
topThreats.action: Severity: 5/5 Unauthenticated command injection, unsigned firmware, and OCPP abuse enable DC fast‑charger takeover and network pivoting. Transportation Energy EVSE CISA Bulletin

descriptions: Exploit Public‑Facing Application (T1190): Zimbra/OWA XSS, F5 APM RCE, GeoServer RCE. Security Advisory
Valid Accounts (T1078) and Authentication Abuse: VPN bypass, FortiGate credential leaks, FMC static creds. Security Advisory
Web Shell (T1505.003) and LOTL: F5 APM webshells; GeoServer/SQL xp_cmdshell abuse. Security Advisory
Command and Control (T1105/T1090): DNS exfiltration; WebSocket/SOCKS5 tunneling; residential/SOHO proxying. Security Advisory
Driver Abuse (BYOVD), DLL Sideloading, and Identity Theft (token/refresh token capture) observed across campaigns. View Article

outlook72h: Expect opportunistic scanning/exploitation of Cisco FMC and F5 APM to continue; prioritize patch windows and compensating controls on management planes. Increased activity against exposed VNC HMIs and weak VPN configurations; preemptively revoke stale sessions and enforce MFA with geo‑controls. Follow‑on identity abuse from OWA/Zimbra intrusions likely; monitor for mailbox permission drift and abnormal EWS traffic. Potential exploitation of EVSE and HMI CVEs as proof‑of‑concepts circulate; pre‑stage network ACLs and out‑of‑band access fallback plans.
